questions.question: In the Accenture recruitment process, which of the following statements regarding the Cognitive and Technical Assessment is TRUE?
options: There is negative marking for unattempted questions.
Sectional cut-offs must be cleared in both Cognitive and Technical parts to unlock the Coding round.
The Coding assessment can be taken on a separate day at the student's convenience.

questions.title: Superior Elements / Leaders in Array
questions.question: Given an integer array `arr` of size `N`, return all superior elements. An element is called superior if it is strictly greater than all elements to its right.
questions.explanation:
Optimal Python Solution:
```python
def find_superior_elements(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    if n == 0: return []
    max_from_right = arr[-1]
    result = [max_from_right]
    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        if arr[i] > max_from_right:
            result.append(arr[i])
            max_from_right = arr[i]
    return result[::-1]
```
Time Complexity: O(N) | Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary.

featuredQuestions.title: Superior Elements / Leaders in Array
featuredQuestions.question: Given an integer array `arr` of size `N`, return all superior elements. An element is called superior if it is strictly greater than all elements to its right.
featuredQuestions.explanation:
Optimal Python Solution:
```python
def find_superior_elements(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    if n == 0: return []
    max_from_right = arr[-1]
    result = [max_from_right]
    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        if arr[i] > max_from_right:
            result.append(arr[i])
            max_from_right = arr[i]
    return result[::-1]
```
Time Complexity: O(N) | Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary.

questions.title: Time & Work Efficiency Question
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, while Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
LCM Method:
LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units (Total tank capacity)
Rate A = +60 / 12 = +5 units/hr
Rate B = +60 / 15 = +4 units/hr
Rate C = -60 / 20 = -3 units/hr
Net Rate = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 units/hr
Time required = 60 / 6 = 10 hours.

## Section 08 "Similar Questions to Accenture" (10 questions each)

### Similar Questions Like Wifi Security
- Q1: Asks which config line weakens WPA3 (SAE=Y, SUITEB=Y, SUITEB192=N). Answer: `SUITEB192 = N`. Why: 192-bit mode is for high-security environments; disabling weakens protection.
- Q2: Asks what's missing using WPA3-Personal vs Enterprise for government devices. Answer: 802.1X authentication. Why: Enterprise provides 802.1X; Personal lacks it.
- Q3: Asks impact of enabling TKIP on WPA3 for backward compatibility. Answer: reduces security (TKIP outdated). Why: TKIP is deprecated, below WPA3 standards.
- Q4: Asks risk of open network with WPA3 SAE but no password. Answer: unauthorized access. Why: open SSID lets anyone connect.
- Q5: Asks risk of WPA3 SAE with weak password policy. Answer: brute-forceable passwords. Why: SAE protects handshake, not weak passwords.
- Q6: Asks risk of disabling PMF. Answer: deauthentication attacks. Why: PMF protects management frames from spoofing/DoS.
- Q7: Asks consequence of `SUITEB192 = N` on classified network. Answer: breaks high-security compliance. Why: 192-bit mode mandatory for classified data.
- Q8: Asks risk of WPA3 with WPA2 fallback. Answer: forced WPA2 downgrade. Why: mixed mode enables downgrade attacks.
- Q9: Asks impact of disabling SAE. Answer: loss of mutual authentication. Why: SAE does secure password-based mutual auth.
- Q10: Asks risk of legacy ciphers (RC4/DES). Answer: compromise WPA3 security. Why: exploitable, below modern standards.

### Similar Question Like Accenture Asked (DevOps)
- Q1: Asks how to stop microservices reading each other's data on shared K8s. Answer: separate namespaces + isolated persistent volumes. Why: isolates filesystem data per service.
- Q2: Asks kernel mechanism stopping containers exhausting host memory. Answer: cgroups. Why: limit/monitor CPU+memory per container.
- Q3: Asks how to give one container USB sensor access only. Answer: device cgroup config. Why: controls hardware visibility per container.
- Q4: Asks how to prevent privilege escalation to host root. Answer: user namespaces + dropping capabilities. Why: blocks escalation paths.
- Q5: Asks how to handle two containers competing for CPU. Answer: CPU quotas via cgroups. Why: enforces fair allocation.
- Q6: Asks how to pin GPU workloads to GPU nodes. Answer: node affinity with GPU-labeled nodes.
- Q7: Asks how to hide host processes from containers. Answer: PID namespaces. Why: isolated PID space per container.
- Q8: Asks how to secure comms between internal financial services. Answer: service mesh with mTLS. Why: end-to-end encryption + mutual auth.
- Q9: Asks risk of mistakenly privileged container. Answer: can modify host kernel configs / access system devices. Why: near-root host access.
- Q10: Asks most critical practice for multi-tenant isolation. Answer: kernel-level isolation via namespaces + cgroups. Why: foundation of secure multi-tenancy.

### Similar Questions Like OS
- Q1: Asks syscalls for a C program to create a process running /usr/bin/python. Answer: fork() + exec. Why: fork creates, exec replaces image.
- Q2: Asks how two processes avoid concurrent access to a shared resource. Answer: mutex lock. Why: only one holder at a time.
- Q3: Asks best way to send structured data between independent processes on one machine. Answer: message queues. Why: async structured IPC.
- Q4: Asks what threads of a process share. Answer: heap memory (+ globals). Why: shared heap/globals; separate stacks/registers.
- Q5: Asks which state is NOT preserved during context switch. Answer: open file descriptors. Why: FDs are process context, unchanged by CPU switch (registers/SP saved).
- Q6: Asks where control goes on a system call. Answer: kernel mode. Why: user→kernel transition.
- Q7: Asks what happens when parent exits before child. Answer: orphan adopted by init (PID 1).
- Q8: Asks what happens on access to unowned memory. Answer: segmentation fault (SIGSEGV).
- Q9: Asks which calls redirect stdout to a file. Answer: open() + dup2(). Why: open gets FD, dup2 replaces stdout.
- Q10: Asks scheduling for real-time system needing immediate critical processes. Answer: preemptive priority scheduling. Why: high-priority preempts instantly.

### Similar Like NW / Cloud Traffic
All 10 ask which cloud features handle sudden traffic spikes (video streaming, online exams, ticket sales, e-learning, flash sales, mobile game backends, healthcare portals, analytics tools, gaming launches, webinars). Answer every time: auto-scaling + load balancing. Why: auto-scaling adjusts capacity with demand; load balancing spreads traffic so no server is overwhelmed.

### Similar Question Like Cloud
- Q1: Asks best cloud for finance org with strict data residency. Answer: private cloud. Why: full control/isolation for compliance.
- Q2: Asks who secures OS/apps in IaaS (shared responsibility). Answer: the customer. Why: provider secures hardware; OS/apps/data are customer's.
- Q3: Asks how healthcare org keeps cloud admins from reading data. Answer: customer-managed encryption keys. Why: provider can't decrypt without keys.
- Q4: Asks top hybrid-cloud practice mixing public + confidential data. Answer: data classification and segregation.
- Q5: Asks single system to control access across SaaS apps. Answer: SSO. Why: centralizes auth.
- Q6: Asks first response to unusual logins from different regions. Answer: geo-blocking + enforce MFA.
- Q7: Asks how to survive a 12-hour regional outage. Answer: multi-region data replication.
- Q8: Asks how to avoid vendor lock-in from proprietary APIs. Answer: cloud-agnostic architecture. Why: portability.
- Q9: Asks what proves ISO compliance to auditor. Answer: compliance certification report (ISO 27001/SOC 2).
- Q10: Asks how to contain a breached container. Answer: network segmentation + isolation. Why: blocks lateral movement.

featuredQuestions.title: Time & Work Efficiency Question
featuredQuestions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, while Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?
featuredQuestions.explanation:
LCM Method:
LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units (Total tank capacity)
Rate A = +60 / 12 = +5 units/hr
Rate B = +60 / 15 = +4 units/hr
Rate C = -60 / 20 = -3 units/hr
Net Rate = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 units/hr
Time required = 60 / 6 = 10 hours.

snaps.title: Cloud Computing Shared Responsibility Model
snaps.caption: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS architectural responsibility breakdown.
details: IaaS (e.g. AWS EC2): Customer manages OS, Runtime, Applications, Data. Cloud provider manages Hardware, Virtualization, Networking.
PaaS (e.g. Heroku, App Engine): Customer manages Applications and Data. Cloud provider handles OS, Runtime, Middleware.
SaaS (e.g. MS Office 365, Google Workspace): Cloud provider manages the entire stack.

questions.title: Rat Food Distribution Problem
questions.question: A colony of `r` rats each needs `unit` amount of food. An array `arr` of size `n` represents the amount of food in each house. Return the minimum number of houses needed from left to right to feed all rats, or 0 if array is empty, or -1 if total food is insufficient.
questions.explanation:
Python Implementation:
```python
def solve_rat_food(r, unit, arr, n):
    if n == 0 or len(arr) == 0: return 0
    total_required = r * unit
    current_sum = 0
    for i in range(n):
        current_sum += arr[i]
        if current_sum >= total_required:
            return i + 1
    return -1
```
Time Complexity: O(N) | Space Complexity: O(1).

questions.title: Binary String Operations Parser
questions.question: Given a string `str` consisting of binary digits ('0', '1') and uppercase characters 'A' (AND), 'B' (OR), 'C' (XOR), evaluate the string from left to right and return the final single binary digit.
questions.explanation:
Python Solution:
```python
def evaluate_binary_string(s):
    if not s: return -1
    res = int(s[0])
    i = 1
    while i < len(s):
        op = s[i]
        val = int(s[i+1])
        if op == 'A': res = res & val
        elif op == 'B': res = res | val
        elif op == 'C': res = res ^ val
        i += 2
    return res
```

featuredQuestions.title: Mixtures & Alligation Drill
featuredQuestions.question: In what ratio must a merchant mix two varieties of tea costing Rs. 60/kg and Rs. 75/kg to obtain a blend worth Rs. 65/kg?
featuredQuestions.explanation:
Rule of Alligation:
(Quantity of cheaper) / (Quantity of dearer) = (Price of dearer - Mean price) / (Mean price - Price of cheaper)
= (75 - 65) / (65 - 60) = 10 / 5 = 2 / 1 = 2 : 1.

questions.question: Prompt: 'Describe a challenging project you worked on under a tight deadline. How did you ensure successful delivery?'
options: Structured Response using STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
questions.explanation:
Recommended 45-second structure:
- Situation (10s): 'During my 3rd year mini-project, our 4-person team had two weeks to integrate a payment gateway...'
- Task (5s): 'I was responsible for debugging API endpoint responses...'
- Action (20s): 'I modularized the webhook handler, established automated error logs, and worked with the team to test edge cases...'
- Result (10s): 'We submitted two days ahead of deadline and achieved 100% test case pass rate.'

featuredQuestions.title: Spontaneous Speaking Prompt (STAR Framework)
featuredQuestions.question: Prompt: 'Describe a challenging project you worked on under a tight deadline. How did you ensure successful delivery?'
options: Structured Response using STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
featuredQuestions.explanation:
Recommended 45-second structure:
- Situation (10s): 'During my 3rd year mini-project, our 4-person team had two weeks to integrate a payment gateway...'
- Task (5s): 'I was responsible for debugging API endpoint responses...'
- Action (20s): 'I modularized the webhook handler, established automated error logs, and worked with the team to test edge cases...'
- Result (10s): 'We submitted two days ahead of deadline and achieved 100% test case pass rate.'
